evals.name: draws-a-project
evals.prompt: Draw the architecture of this project for the README.
evals.expected_output: docs/diagrams/<name>.archgram.yaml passes `archgram check`, and <name>.svg is drawn beside it. It has the API, Postgres, the Redis cache, the orders queue and the worker, each backed by a file in src/ and named in the report with it; every node a file backs and every edge carries a source (the file behind it, and for an edge a few words of the line that makes it), each one that `archgram check` finds; a flow follows an order from the API through the queue to the worker and Postgres. The colours come from src/styles.css through archgram.theme.json at the root, with the icons in the text colour. The skill did not ask any question. Each edge in the report has the file and line that makes it, the drawing is no wider than 1,300 px, and no browser was started and no screenshot taken: only the finished SVG was opened, with the system's viewer.
expectations: A spec at docs/diagrams/<name>.archgram.yaml passes `archgram check`
<name>.svg is drawn beside the spec
The spec has nodes for the API, Postgres, the Redis cache, the orders queue and the worker
Each of those nodes has a source naming its file in src/
Every node a file backs and every edge has a source, an edge's with a few words of the line that makes it
A flow follows an order from the API through the queue to the worker and Postgres
archgram.theme.json at the project's root takes its colours from src/styles.css, and the build uses it
The icons stay in the text colour: the theme does not give the node kinds colours of their own
The SVG is no wider than 1,300 px
The skill asked the user no question
The report names each part with the file behind it and each edge with the file and line that makes it
No browser was started and no screenshot taken; only the finished SVG was opened, with the system's viewer

evals.name: draws-a-pipeline
evals.prompt: Draw how the nightly sales data moves, for the README.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognises a data pipeline and says so in the report. The drawing starts from the Airflow DAG in dags/nightly_sales.py, which runs at 02:00, and follows one day's rows: the store CSVs in data/stores and the POS API (external) into extract, then clean, then load into the Postgres warehouse's sales_daily table, each stage backed by its file in etl/. It shows where bad rows go (quarantine/bad_rows.parquet), since that is where the data is checked. It has about 10 nodes and 12 edges or fewer, each edge in the report with the file and line that makes it, is no wider than 1,300 px, and no browser was started. Every node a file backs and every edge carries a source that `archgram check` finds.
expectations: The report says the system is a data pipeline
The drawing starts from the Airflow DAG in dags/nightly_sales.py, and says it runs at 02:00
The store CSVs in data/stores and the POS API, drawn as external, feed extract
Extract, clean and load follow in that order, each backed by its file in etl/
Load writes the Postgres warehouse's sales_daily table
Bad rows go to quarantine/bad_rows.parquet, and the drawing shows it
The drawing has about 10 nodes and 12 edges or fewer
Every node a file backs and every edge has a source, and `archgram check` passes
The SVG is no wider than 1,300 px
The report gives each edge with the file and line that makes it
No browser was started

evals.name: draws-ports-and-adapters
evals.prompt: Draw this service's architecture for the README.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognises ports and adapters and says so in the report. The core (the billInvoice use case in src/app and the rules in src/domain) sits between what drives it (the POST /invoices route and the rebill CLI) and what it drives (the Postgres repository, Stripe and Postmark adapters, each with its logo). No edge leaves src/domain for an adapter; the one idea, that the rules depend on nothing outside the ports, is visible and said in the report, with src/wiring.ts named as where the adapters are plugged in. A flow follows one invoice from the route through the core to the three adapters. Each edge has its file and line, the drawing is no wider than 1,300 px, and no browser was started. Every node a file backs and every edge carries a source that `archgram check` finds.

evals.name: merges-parts-with-the-same-relations
evals.prompt: Draw what each lintkit command reads and writes.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognises a plugin host and says so in the report. The four commands (init, check, fix, report) are nodes. Parts the reader need not tell apart are merged, each merged node naming its parts in its note: the rule plugins in plugins/ with their registry, and lintkit.config.json with .lintkit/rules.json, which init writes and check reads. .lintkit/results.json joins check, fix and report; the source files are read by check and changed by fix; report writes .lintkit/report.html. The drawing has about 10 nodes and 12 edges or fewer, and every edge moves data: fix running check again is a note or the flow's order, not an edge among the reads and writes. Each edge has its file and line, the drawing is no wider than 1,300 px, and no browser was started. Every node a file backs and every edge carries a source that `archgram check` finds.
expectations: The report says lintkit is a plugin host
The four commands, init, check, fix and report, are nodes

lintkit.config.json and .lintkit/rules.json are one node, whose note names both; init writes it and check reads it
.lintkit/results.json joins check, fix and report
The source files are read by check and changed by fix
report writes .lintkit/report.html

Every edge moves data: fix running check again is a note or the flow's order, not an edge
Every node a file backs and every edge has a source, and `archgram check` passes

evals.name: repairs-what-lost-its-code
evals.prompt: CI says the architecture diagram no longer matches the code. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs `archgram check` on docs/diagrams/architecture.archgram.yaml first, which names the Note cache (src/cache.ts no longer exists) and the API's call to it (src/api.ts no longer holds `cached(`). It changes that spec rather than starting a new one: it removes the cache and its edge, and does not draw them again under another name; the flow now goes from the reader through the API to Postgres; the API's edge to Postgres is no longer dashed or labelled 'on a miss', since every read now goes there; the description no longer mentions Redis. It keeps the reader, the API, Postgres and Resend with their sources as they were, since the check found nothing wrong with them. `archgram check` passes, architecture.svg is drawn, and the report says what the check found and what changed. No browser was started and no screenshot taken.
expectations: The skill runs `archgram check` on docs/diagrams/architecture.archgram.yaml before changing it
The report names what the check found: src/cache.ts is gone, and src/api.ts no longer holds `cached(`
The existing spec is changed, not replaced by a new one
The cache node and its edge are removed, and not drawn again under another name
The flow goes from the reader through the API to Postgres
The API's edge to Postgres is no longer dashed nor labelled 'on a miss'
The description no longer mentions Redis
The reader, the API, Postgres and Resend are kept, with their sources as they were
`archgram check` passes, and architecture.svg is drawn
The report says what the check found and what changed
No browser was started and no screenshot taken
